subject: general
question: Which of the following dance forms incorporates the most intricate makeup code, costume, face masks, headdress and brightly painted faces?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A significant type **of **classical Indian dance **is **kathakali**.
 
• The **extremely colourful make-**up**, costumes**, and **face masks **that the **traditionally male actor-dancers wear **set this **"story play" **kind of **art apart**.
 
• The **seventeenth century **saw the development of **Kathakali, **or "tale drama," in **Kerala, southern India**, with the **support of the prince of Karnataka**.
 
• **Women execute **the **dance in homage **to the **Hindu god Vishnu**, who is represented by the **enchantress Mohini**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One of the eight primary styles **of **Indian classical **dance is **kathak**. It is **Uttar Pradesh's traditional style **of **dance**. **Traditional accounts trace **the **development **of **Kathak **to the **wandering storytellers **known as **Kathakars **in **ancient northern India**.
 
• **Indian traditional dance **known as **Sattriya **is very popular. It is a dance-drama performance art that has its **roots in the Krishna-centered Vaishnavism monasteries **of **Assam **and is credited to the **saint and scholar of the Bhakti movement Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev**, who lived in **the 15th century**.
 
• **Odissi**, also referred to as **Orissi in old literature**, is a **major ancient Indian classical dance **that originated in the **temples of Odisha **– an eastern coastal state of India.
